grand_strategy.reading: Federated States of Micronesia runs its foreign policy inside a treaty: the Compact with the United States, renewed and funded in 2024 with US$3.3 billion over 20 years, is the anchor, and the one stance here sourced at B. Its second relation, with Beijing since 1989, is a small trade and aid tie whose recent record this pass did not read, and the other two Compact states (Marshall Islands and Palau), Japan, Australia and the Pacific Islands Forum are open gaps. The one dated action read so far, the September 2025 vote against the New York Declaration, shows the Compact alignment at work in the UN.

stances.note: Ally by treaty. The Compact of Free Association with the United States is a treaty, renewed and funded in 2024 with US$3.3 billion over 20 years, through 2043 (Interior Department). The grade follows the treaty, not the rhetoric. Since is the renewal year: the 1986 entry into force is not sourced in this pass. Trend stable: no 2025-26 change was read. Bond affinity is our reading, not sourced here: close ties without kinship. Confidence B: one tier-1 source, the Interior press release, not the treaty text. The defence and visa terms of the Compact are not written, because no source for them was read.

stances.note: Partner, transactional, with no alignment read. Relations date from 11 September 1989 (FSM mission table) and the government marked twenty years of them in 2009, with China as third-largest trade partner and about US$9.5 million of trade in 2007 (government release, 2009). Bond none is our reading: no kinship and no open grievance was read. Trend stable is a default, because no 2022-26 source was read: the Chinese police help, the 'all-round' wording and any 2023 warnings from the government are not written here. Confidence C: the sources are pre-2022 and the 2009 release was read through the Wikipedia index, not fetched directly.

stances_toward.note: Partner, not ally: there is no treaty between the two, but the DOI describes the Micronesia and Marshall Islands Compacts as the two that carry the first financial commitment from 1986 (DOI, read in full). In February 2021 the two left the Pacific Islands Forum together, with Kiribati and Nauru, in a joint statement (RNZ, cited by Wikipedia; not opened). Bond affinity: a shared Compact and a joint walkout, with no kinship read; no source gave the kin reading.
